samples.summary: PUT /content accepts read-scoped API keys — no `write` scope gate, unlike the sibling v1 mutating endpoints
samples.evidence: `ApiKey.scopes` is a real capability: `CreateApiKeyDto` (packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.dto.ts:12-25) lets an owner mint a key with `scopes: ['read']`, `ApiKeyStrategy.validate` puts it on `req.user.scopes` (api-key.strategy.ts:25), and two other v1 handlers enforce it — `documents.controller.ts:108` (`if (!req.user.scopes?.includes('write')) throw new ForbiddenException(...)`) and `files.controller.ts:80` whose comment says outright "Without this a read-scoped key could create documents." `ApiV1DocsContentController.putContent` (docs-content.controller.ts:126-199) is guarded only by `CombinedAuthGuard` + `WorkspaceScopeGuard`; the scope guard checks *workspace identity* only (workspace-scope.guard.ts:26-32) and neither guard reads `scopes` (grep for `scopes` across packages/backend/src returns no hit in this controller or in combined-auth.guard.ts). Attack: hold a `['read']`-scoped `wfb_…` key for a workspace, `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/content` with any valid body — `writeSlidesRoot`/`writeDocsRoot`/`writeNoteRoot` are a documented *destructive replace* (slides-tree.ts:87-92, "every top-level slides field on the root is overwritten"), so a read-only credential silently gains full write/destroy over every doc, deck and note in the workspace. The same omission covers cells.controller.ts:105/131/150, tabs.controller.ts:80/103, images.controller.ts:35/99 and documents.controller.ts:48/79, so the pattern is systemic and the two existing checks make the surface read as covered.

samples.summary: The new absent-`data` repair covers only `type === 'text'`; every other element type still persists with no `data` and TypeErrors in every viewer
samples.evidence: The delta adds a repair so a text element without `data` is stored as `{ blocks: [] }`, then falls through to the pre-existing guard `if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;` (line 640) for all other types. But the renderer dereferences `element.data` unconditionally for *every* type: `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/element-renderer.ts:257` (`element.data.effects?.shadow`) runs for shape/image/table/chart, :200-201 (`element.data.refSize`) and :241 (`for (const child of element.data.children)`) run for groups — none of them optional-chained on `data` itself, and `drawElementBody` only wraps the paint in `try/finally` (no catch, line 191), so the throw escapes the whole slide render. Attack: any caller with write access PUTs `{"id":"e1","type":"group","frame":{}}` (or `type:"image"`, or `type:"group", data:[]` — an array passes `typeof data === 'object'` and `data.children` is then undefined). The validator accepts it, `writeSlidesRoot` stores it verbatim, `migrateElement` (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:155-156) repairs shapes only — so the deck is now unrenderable for every viewer of the workspace, a persistent, stored denial of service. The delta's own rest-api.md hunk claims "no deck is ever persisted in a shape that would be a TypeError for its viewers", which makes the remaining hole read as closed.

samples.summary: Table-element repair fills in `cell.body` but leaves `cell.style`, `columnWidths` and non-object cells/rows unrepaired — the same stored-crash it claims to close
samples.evidence: The new cell loop repairs an absent `body` (line 654-662) but skips any cell that is null or an array (`line 653: continue`) and never touches `cell.style` or `data.columnWidths`. `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts` reads all of these unconditionally, and *earlier* in the same pass than the body it repairs: line 41 `data.columnWidths.length` (crashes on `{"type":"table","frame":{},"data":{}}`, which this validator accepts because `rows` is coerced via `Array.isArray(data.rows) ? data.rows : []`), line 100/201 `row.cells[c]` (a row with no `cells` array is skipped by the validator at line 650 and crashes here), and line 203 `cell.style.fill` (a cell with a `body` but no `style` passes validation and TypeErrors before the repaired `cell.body.blocks` at line 229 is ever reached). Attack: PUT a deck with such a table; it is stored verbatim (`writeSlidesRoot`) and no read-side migration repairs it (`migrateElement` handles shapes only), so every viewer's render of that slide throws — persistent DoS. The added repair makes the path read as hardened while the adjacent required fields on the exact loop it rewrote are still unguarded.

samples.summary: `LAYOUT_ID_MIGRATIONS[slide?.layoutId]` is a plain-object lookup keyed by attacker-controlled data — the exact prototype-chain pattern this branch claims it swept
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlide` (docs-content.controller.ts:528) accepts any non-empty string for `layoutId`, and `writeSlidesRoot` stores it verbatim. On read, `migrateSlide` does `LAYOUT_ID_MIGRATIONS[slide?.layoutId] ?? slide?.layoutId ?? 'blank'` against a `Record<string,string>` object literal (migrate.ts:8). `layoutId: "constructor"` yields the `Object` constructor function, `"__proto__"` yields `Object.prototype`, `"toString"`/`"valueOf"` yield functions — so a field typed `string` becomes a function/object inside the live model and flows on into `doc.layouts.find(l => l.id === slide.layoutId)` (presentation.ts:215/231), `layoutEditSlideId` string interpolation (layout.ts:245) and `layoutIdToPath.get(slide.layoutId)` in the PPTX exporter (export/pptx/index.ts:341), plus any re-serialization of the migrated slide back into Yorkie. This is the same defect class the branch's own lessons file records for `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` and explicitly warns is under-swept ("grep the pass for the pattern, don't trust the prose", docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:143); this lookup was not converted to a `Map`. I could not complete a chain past type confusion / crash to a stronger impact, hence low confidence.

samples.summary: Unbounded recursion in the element walk with a 25MB JSON body limit — cheap CPU/stack DoS on an authenticated endpoint
samples.evidence: `assertValidElementData` recurses into `data.children` via `assertValidNestedElement` (line 673) with no depth cap, and `assertValidBlock`/`assertValidSlideBlocks` recurse through nested table blocks. `bodyParser.json({ limit: JSON_BODY_LIMIT })` in packages/backend/src/main.ts:49 uses the 25MB content-import limit (see comment at :46), so a body of ~90 bytes per nesting level buys hundreds of thousands of levels of `{"type":"group","data":{"children":[…]}}`. Result is a `RangeError` surfaced as a 500 plus the parse/walk cost, repeatable at the 120 req/min throttle. Caught exceptions mean no process crash, so impact is limited to resource burn and noisy 500s — hardening suggestion, not an outage.

verdict.reason: Independently verified: PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/content is guarded only by CombinedAuthGuard + WorkspaceScopeGuard, neither of which reads ApiKey scopes, and putContent takes no request object so it cannot check them either. `scopes` is a genuine capability (ApiKeyService.create honors caller-supplied scopes; ApiKeyStrategy.validate puts them on req.user) and is enforced at exactly two sites in the entire backend (documents.controller.ts:105-110 and files.controller.ts:80, per an exhaustive `isApiKey` grep). I searched for a counterexample in every indirect path: no global guard (app.module.ts registers only ThrottlerGuard as APP_GUARD; main.ts sets no global guards), no module-scoped guard in api-v1.module.ts, no scope check in ApiKeyService.validateKey, and no @RequireScope-style decorator or method-based (GET vs mutating) scope gate anywhere. A read-scoped workspace key therefore passes both guards and reaches writeDocsRoot/writeSlidesRoot/writeNoteRoot, a destructive whole-document replace — privilege escalation from a read-only credential to full write/destroy. Missing authorization gate on a mutating endpoint, in the Security lane, critical impact.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The table branch of assertValidElementData (docs-content.controller.ts:646-669) repairs only cell.body: rows are coerced via `Array.isArray(data.rows) ? data.rows : []` (647), rows without a `cells` array are silently skipped (650), null/array cells are skipped (653), and neither `cell.style` nor `data.columnWidths` is validated anywhere in the backend (grep: no `columnWidths` hit in packages/backend). assertValidElement (560-581) demands only id/type/frame, so `{"id":"x","type":"table","frame":{},"data":{}}` is accepted. The slides renderer dereferences precisely those unrepaired fields, and earlier than the repaired one: table-renderer.ts:41 `data.columnWidths.length` is the first statement of drawTable; computeTableLayout:100 `row.cells[c]` and :581 `cell.style.padding` run at line 44 before any body read; paintCellFills:201/203 `row.cells[c]` / `cell.style.fill` run before paintCellContents:229 `cell.body.blocks`. Reachability confirmed: element-renderer.ts:356 calls drawTable unconditionally for type 'table', and migrate.ts:155-156 `migrateElement` returns non-shape elements untouched, so nothing repairs the stored shape on read; slides-tree.ts:16-19 documents writeSlidesRoot as a destructive verbatim replace. An authenticated workspace writer can therefore persist a deck that TypeErrors in every viewer's render — stored denial of service from unsanitized input, on the same loop the change hardened. No refutation ground applies (code present as described, no guard, in-lane as unsafe input handling with persistent availability impact).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo, and every element of the claim checks out. migrate.ts:8 declares LAYOUT_ID_MIGRATIONS as a plain object literal (`Record<string,string>`), and migrate.ts:122 indexes it with `slide?.layoutId`, an untrusted key: `LAYOUT_ID_MIGRATIONS['constructor']` resolves through Object.prototype to the Object constructor function, which is non-nullish and therefore survives both `??` fallbacks and is assigned to `migrated.layoutId` (line 125), a field typed `string`. The key is attacker-controllable: assertValidSlide (docs-content.controller.ts:528-532) accepts any non-empty string for layoutId with no allowlist or membership check against the deck's layouts, and putContent (docs-content.controller.ts:189-198) hands the body straight to writeSlidesRoot unmodified, so the value is persisted verbatim and re-enters migrateSlide on every read. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as quoted (not-present fails); migrateSlide IS the read-path normalizer and nothing upstream or downstream constrains layoutId to a closed set before the lookup — consumers at presentation.ts:215/231, export/pptx/index.ts:341 and layout.ts:245 receive the already-corrupted value (already-guarded fails); and untrusted-input handling that reaches a prototype-chain lookup is squarely in the security lane's 'unsafe input handling' category (out-of-scope fails). The repository itself treats this precise pattern as a security defect requiring a fix: export/pptx/color.ts:19-30 converted the sibling ROLE_TO_SCHEME lookup to a Map with a comment explaining that the Record form 'reaches the prototype chain' and stringifies the Object constructor into output, and docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:131-145 records the class and warns the sweep is under-applied. migrate.ts:122 is a lookup that sweep missed. The reviewer's low confidence concerns how far the impact chain extends, not whether the vector exists.
